research_metadata.title: ECDSA Research: Algebraic Coincidences and Anomalies in Signatures
research_metadata.status: Active research journal — documented dead-end for real secp256k1
research_metadata.purpose: Investigation of algebraic artifacts/anomalies in ECDSA signatures that allow deterministic private key recovery on small-order test curves. Current focus: deep analysis of subclasses D[i] on already generated legacy secp256k1 transaction dataset.
research_metadata.core_finding: No new vulnerability on secp256k1. All observed phenomena are statistical coincidences with probability O(1/n) that vanish on large curves.

curve_parameters.description: Standard secp256k1 and reduced test curves used for experiments

hidden_decomposition.s_zk: z · k⁻¹  (mod n)   — hidden hash/nonce component
hidden_decomposition.s_rxk: r · x · k⁻¹  (mod n) — hidden key component
hidden_decomposition.recovery_formula: x = z · (s − s_zk) · (r · s_zk)⁻¹  (mod n)   [exact only when s_zk is the true value]

publicly_derivable_values.a: s mod ((s_zr − s) mod n)   — key value used in classification

A.name: Class A
A.condition: m1 = s_zk / a is integer and m1 == 1
A.description: s_zk exactly equals a (the publicly computed value)
A.recovery: Direct: x = _recover_private_key_case_a(s, z, r, a, n)
A.example_from_data: Observed on tiny curve; very rare on larger curves

B.name: Class B
B.condition: m1 = s_zk / a and m2 = (s + s_zr) / s_rxk are both integers and m1 == m2 > 1
B.description: Both fractions are integers and equal (quadratic relation)
B.recovery: Solve modular quadratic equation for m1, then recover x (up to 2 candidates)
B.example_from_data: Extremely rare; almost never observed on curves larger than tiny

C.name: Class C
C.condition: m1 = s_zk / a is integer > 1, but m1 != m2 or m2 not integer

D.name: Class D (and subclasses D[i])
D.condition: m1 = s_zk / a is NOT an integer (fractional). Level N = floor(f) where f = s_zk / a
D.description: Most common class. Uses floor of the ratio to define a search window for s_zk: [a·N, a·(N+1)]
D.recovery: No direct closed-form. Requires searching the window [a·N, a·(N+1)]. Cross-transaction intersection possible when multiple tx share the same x.
D.frequency: Dominant (~25% of all transactions that satisfy s_zr > s)
D.window_definition: For a given transaction with computed a and f = s_zk / a: N = floor(f), search s_zk in range [a·N, a·(N+1)]

E.name: Class E (Goldbach-like)
E.description: Symmetric pair around s/2 with fixed difference floor(s/2)+1. Two candidate values for s_zk: α = (s + floor(s/2) + 1)//2 and β = s − α
E.recovery: Two candidates using case A formula on α and β
E.important_note: The '+1' offset is arbitrary. Control experiments with other offsets (+3, +5, -1, etc.) yield the same frequency. Not privileged.
E.example_from_data: Observed on tiny and small curves; drops to zero on large curve

class_D_detailed.definition: Transactions where Fraction(s_zk, a) is not an integer. The integer part N = floor(s_zk / a) defines the 'level' or subclass D[N].

search_window.note: When N=0 the effective window starts from 1 to a (special handling)

class_D_detailed.why_circular_on_real_secp256k1: To know the correct N you need to know secret s_zk. Without it you must try all possible N, which is equivalent to brute-forcing O(n).
class_D_detailed.current_research_direction: Deep mining of already generated legacy secp256k1 D[i] transactions for hidden statistical patterns, biases in distribution of i, correlations between fields inside same D[i], and possible secondary structures that could allow better window narrowing than plain floor(f).

frequency_table.description: Observed counts of anomaly classes across different curve sizes (confirms O(1/n) scaling)

D_subclass_distribution.higher_D: Counts continue to decrease; many D>100 with count 1-3
D_subclass_distribution.note: Distribution follows expected decay as level N increases

common_x_recovery_demo.note: Demonstrates that when multiple transactions share the same private key, intersecting their D-windows can recover x on small curves.

class_D_hypotheses.description: Collection of mathematical hypotheses specifically for Class D (and its subclasses D[i]). Each hypothesis aims to find additional structure inside D transactions that could allow better narrowing of the s_zk search window or reveal non-random patterns. Hypotheses are tracked with status for evolution monitoring.

applies_to.notes: Hypothesis applies exclusively to Class D transactions whose floor(f) level is greater than 1.

HYP-005.title: Relation between a and w = s_zk - N·a when s_zk is even and s > s_zk
HYP-005.description: For D transactions where the level N > 1, s > s_zk and s_zk is even, there may exist a recoverable relation that verifies the correctness of a using w = s_zk − N·a.
HYP-005.mathematical_formulation:
w = s_zk - N · a

a_found = N · w - ((N · a % w) - ((N + 1) · a % w))

If a_found == a → hypothesis holds for this transaction
HYP-005.expected_benefit: Potential way to verify or strengthen the candidate a without knowing s_zk. Could be used as a filter or additional constraint when searching windows across multiple transactions.
HYP-005.verification_method: Run on all D[i] transactions (i > 1) in legacy dataset and count how often a_found == a.
HYP-005.conclusion: Partially observable in code. Requires large-scale statistical verification on the 2523 D cases to determine if it holds significantly more often than random chance.
HYP-005.notes: This is currently the only formalized hypothesis for Class D. It needs rigorous frequency analysis.

key_examples.class_E_note: The Goldbach '+1' structure is not special. Any fixed offset yields similar frequency.

main_conclusions: The recovery formula x = z·(s−s_zk)·(r·s_zk)⁻¹ is a tautology — it works only if you already know the correct s_zk (i.e., the nonce).
Classes A, B, E occur with probability O(1/n) and become negligible on secp256k1.
Class D (~25%) is the most common but the window-narrowing method is circular on large curves.
No evidence of exploitable bias or structure beyond statistical coincidence has been found.
The '~25% anomaly rate' is an arithmetic property of modular comparison, not an exploit indicator.
honest_assessment_and_conclusions.what_would_be_a_real_result: Finding a class whose frequency significantly exceeds the expected c/n baseline across large samples — indicating a genuine bias in the distribution of s_zk.

current_research_direction.focus: Deep analysis of subclasses D[i] in the legacy secp256k1 dataset (2523 D cases).
goals: Search for statistical anomalies or non-uniform distribution in the levels i (D0, D1, D2, ...)
Look for correlations between fields (z, r, s, a, f) within the same D[i]
Investigate possible secondary algebraic structures inside D[i] that could allow better than O(a) window narrowing
Compare behavior of D[i] across test curves vs real secp256k1
